title: Chargers start/sit: Week 2 fantasy football outlook - NewsBreak
text:
By Spencer Schultz ,
32 minutes ago [US, Mexico & Canada customers only] Sep 5, 2025; Sao Paulo, BRAZIL; Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) during the warm up before a NFL game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Corinthians Arena. Mandatory Credit: Amanda Perobelli/Reuters via Imagn Images By Amanda Perobelli, REUTERS What an impressive performance from the Chargers in the season opener, particularly from the offense. While it's still only been one game, the game showed the potential of this offense in 2025.
Let's translate that to fantasy football and see who should be considered a start/sit in Week 2.
Start: QB Justin Herbert
Herbert sent a message in the season opener with 318 passing yards, 32 rushing yards, and three touchdowns against one of the league's best defenses. Until proven otherwise, he is a viable starter in most weeks, and that holds especially true against a defense like the Raiders .
Sit: WR Quentin Johnston
There's no doubt that the former first-rounder looked like a potential breakout star in Week 1. The former TCU product finished with 79 receiving yards and two touchdowns, and things get even easier against Las Vegas' secondary this weekend. Despite that, he is going to need to prove it for a few more weeks before he should be regularly started. In deeper leagues, though, slotting him into your flex spot isn't a bad idea.
Start: WR Ladd McConkey
McConkey picked up right where he left off from his rookie campaign with a stellar six catches for 74 yards in the opener. He remains Herbert's favorite target, and that should be the case for the duration of the 2025 campaign. McConkey should be considered a must-start no matter the matchup at this point.
Sit: Tight ends
At this point, there are too many mouths to feed in this offense. That doesn't leave much room for a viable tight end option for fantasy, and that likely won't change this year. Will Dissly and Tyler Conklin combined for just three catches and 68 yards in Week 1, with the latter one as the better option if absolutely needed.
Start: RB Omarion Hampton
The rookie's debut came with a mixed bag as Hampton averaged just 3.2 yards per carry on 15 attempts. While he failed to reach the endzone, he still finished with 17 total touches and played 80% of the team's offensive snaps. While the volume is there, you have to be patient and the production will eventually come. The Raiders did hold the Patriots to just 3.3 yards per attempt for 60 rushing yards in Week 1, but don't let that keep you from starting Hampton this week.
Start: WR Keenan Allen
Welcome back to Los Angeles, Mr. Allen. It was a stellar performance in his first game back with the Chargers as he finished with seven catches for 68 yards and a touchdown. Allen led the team with 10 targets and was targeted regularly in key situations by Herbert. Those two picked up right where they left off in 2023, and the connection was still there like nothing had happened.
